text: In C-CAT, this concept shows up as conceptual, definition-based questions. Expect to be asked to pick the correct definition of programming, or to tell apart terms that sound almost the same — especially program versus programming. Keep the anchor in your head: programming is the process, a program is the product. A question might also describe a task and ask what a computer needs in order to perform it — and the answer it's looking for is a clear, ordered set of instructions, not intelligence or guesswork on the computer's part.
